decks.name: Collecting · 收藏
decks.description: IELTS-style article: why people collect things (4 paragraphs, 23 vocabulary cards)

cards.back:
v. 收集；收藏
e.g. People collect all sorts of things.

n. 冰箱贴
e.g. I collect fridge magnets, so my fridge has slowly become a colourful map.

n. 美好的回忆
e.g. I have fond memories of collecting rocks and shells from the beach.

n. 纪念品
e.g. Others bring home souvenirs from their travels.

n. 化石
e.g. Some people collect natural objects such as fossils and interesting stones.

adj. 微型的；缩小的
e.g. People collect miniature versions of real commercial products.

adj. 按比例缩小的
e.g. scaled-down retro toys, classic board games and action figures.

adj. 复古的
e.g. scaled-down retro toys.

n. 可动人偶；手办
e.g. scaled-down retro toys, classic board games and action figures.

n./adj. 收藏品；值得收藏的
e.g. Collectables can be both decorative and functional.

adj. 怀旧的；怀念的
e.g. Giving us something nostalgic to look at or fiddle with.

phr. 摆弄；拨弄
e.g. Something nostalgic to look at or fiddle with when bored.

n. 成就感
e.g. Collecting gives us a sense of order and achievement.

phr. 有掌控感；处于掌控之中
e.g. Collecting can help people feel more in control.

n. 身份的延伸
e.g. Collections can become an extension of our identity.

n. 极简主义
e.g. Advocates of minimalism argue that owning fewer possessions improves wellbeing.

v. 囤积
e.g. Filling our homes with collections can seem like unnecessarily hoarding clutter.

n. 杂物；杂乱
e.g. Filling our homes with collections can seem like hoarding clutter.

v. 精心挑选；策展
e.g. There is a distinction between thoughtfully curating your collection and accumulating.

v. 积累；积聚
e.g. Thoughtfully curating your collection vs. simply accumulating more possessions.

n. 过度消费
e.g. Some collectors can be drawn into excessive spending.

adj. 稀有的；罕见的
e.g. Companies release new or rare additions to collections.

n. 自画像
e.g. Happiful describes collections as a kind of self-portrait.
